news.title: Unity EURO Cup 2026 brings record 22 teams together in Coverciano to celebrate inclusion through football
news.lede: The fifth edition of the tournament organised by UEFA and in partnership with UNHCR took place on 15 October at the Italian Football Federation’s technical centre, bringing together refugees and players from host communities across Europe. The Unity EURO Cup returned on 15 October for its fifth edition, with a record 22 teams gathering at Coverciano, the Italian Football Federation’s iconic national technical centre near Florence. Organised by UEFA and in partnership with UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency, the tournament celebrates the power of football to unite people from different backgrounds and support the social inclusion of refugees. This year’s edition featured four more teams than in 2025, reflecting the continued growth of the initiative and its reach across Europe.

news.title: FIFA to Amend Disciplinary Rules After Folarin Balogun World Cup Ban Controversy
news.lede: FIFA has announced plans to amend its disciplinary regulations following controversy over the suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun’s automatic one-match ban, which allowed him to feature against Belgium in their FIFA World Cup last-16 clash. The decision follows concerns raised by the Royal Belgian Football Association (RBFA) over the circumstances surrounding FIFA’s decision to suspend the sanction and the potential implications for the independence and transparency of its disciplinary process. According to the Belgian federation, FIFA will revise Article 27 of its Disciplinary Code, which permits the suspension of disciplinary sanctions under exceptional circumstances. The proposed amendment is expected to be submitted for approval at the next FIFA Council meeting scheduled for December 16 in Doha, Qatar.

news.title: U17 World Cup: NFF Cautions Flamingos Against Match-Fixing
news.lede: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has warned members of the U17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, against match-fixing and other integrity violations ahead of the 2026 FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup. The warning followed a mandatory integrity briefing organised by the NFF Integrity Unit on Wednesday for players and officials selected for the tournament. According to the Federation, the session was designed to help the team recognise attempts to manipulate matches, understand the risks involved and know how to respond to suspicious approaches.

news.lede: Trump's intervention sparked a great deal of controversy, and the international federation is paying the price. news.title: Gianni Infantino issues public apology as FIFA announces massive $6.35 billion investment plan following World Cup success
news.lede: Massive funding package unveiledFIFA President Infantino issued a public apology following the latest FIFA Council meeting at the Home of FIFA in Zurich. The chief executive addressed past mistakes regarding the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which has now been permanently withdrawn.Despite the governance setback, FIFA presented a landmark financial initiative called the FIFA Surplus Solidarity Programme. Driven by exceptional commercial returns from the 48-team 2026 World Cup, the plan will more than double development funding for the 2027-2030 period.The total support package will reach $6.35 billion, drawing from an estimated cycle surplus of between $5.2 billion and $5.6 billion. Infantino took responsibility for how the project was handled and communicated to the global football community."

news.title: Lautaro Martínez debunks conspiracy theories about the World Cup final won by Spain
news.lede: Lautaro Martínez, forward for Inter Milan, dismantles all the speculation and conspiracy theories that were published in Argentina about the 2026 World Cup final, which Spain ended up winning 1-0 thanks to a historic goal by Ferran Torres. After losing the World Cup final, the commitment of the Albiceleste players was even called into question in Argentina. '"When people talk about those theories, it's annoying. The opponent was superior and at some point it was bound to happen," highlighted Lautaro Martínez, who did not play a single second in the final by Scaloni's decision despite being decisive with a goal against England in the semifinals.'

news.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at FIFA meeting over World Cup plan
news.lede: Updated Oct. 16, 2026, 9:18 a.m. FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised for mistakes surrounding a failed plan to bring private investors into the World Cup, but Council members say key questions remain unanswered. FIFA president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project. "We asked a great many critical questions, but there were no satisfactory answers from my point of view," said Bernd Neuendorf, the head of the German Football Association (DFB), who is also a member of the FIFA Council.
